rationale: bugs_open/265: a component's input_schema has a house dialect ({"fields": {...}}) and a retired JSON-Schema dialect ({"type":"object","properties":{...},"required":[...]}). A code comment in datahelpers/component_schema_fields.go declared the retired dialect EXTINCT fleet-wide (0 of 173, 2026-07-21). Measured 2026-08-16: it has been reintroduced FOUR times since — seeds 207 (2026-07-25, four days after the census), 247 and 250 (2026-07-28), and a hand seed on 2026-08-10 (loans-consolidation, since converted by its own lane on 08-15). Three legacy rows are live now. EVERY one was hand-authored SQL: created_from='manual', source_agent_type NULL; the component-creator (created_from='generated', 69 rows) has produced 0 legacy rows in its life. So the bug file's own guess that the producer was the component-creator was the wrong direction, and no Go-side gate on that path would have stopped a single one of the four. Components are routinely written by migrations and by hand with no commit at all (RFC_009's CronJob header says exactly this) — the only seam that sees every producer is the table. The tripwire that should have surfaced the reintroduction (WarnLegacyDialect, six call sites) writes only a Warn line on agent-chassis, which nobody reads; four rows passed six tripwires for up to 15 days unseen. The fix makes the bad state UNREPRESENTABLE rather than detected: (1) migration 437 converts the three rows to v2 by the exact projection SchemaContentFields already applies (behaviour-preserving, proven by a Go test over the live before/after JSON) and adds CHECK constraint chk_input_schema_no_legacy_dialect refusing a top-level "properties" key for every producer; (2) the one LLM producer (store_generated_component) refuses the same predicate before its write with a message naming the fix, instead of dying on SQLSTATE 23514 after deriveRenderMode has already mis-read the schema as 'template'; (3) the stale census comment is replaced by the constraint (checkable at any moment), the tripwire's message says what a firing now MEANS (the constraint is gone) and moves Warn->Error, and the stale prior-art pointer bugs_open/026 -> bugs_closed/026 is corrected. NOT done: no new CronJob (RFC_006's daily-check pattern is for invariants the DB cannot express; this one it can); the reader's legacy projection is KEPT as defence in depth (deleting it restores the fail-OPEN blind spot bug 026 was opened about); the three applied seeds are not rewritten (history — a hand re-run now fails loudly on the constraint, which is the intended behaviour); report-dossier's source is NOT corrected (its seed says the body is never LLM-authored, the projection marks it llm — the over-report bug 265 addendum 1 predicted; that is its owning lane's content decision, surfaced in the bug file). Scope: this strengthens what a shared table guarantees. Consumers named: writers of input_schema are store_generated_component_action.go (INSERT :528, UPDATE :466), deploy_tool_action.go:303 (copies an existing row's schema — transitively safe), the LMC/loancalculator decomposition loaders (Python, write v2), and any seed; readers all go through SchemaContentFields or ["fields"]. Nothing live writes the retired dialect except hand seeds, which is the point.

plan.summary: Migration 437: guard (not already applied; population is exactly the 3 named rows by id; every property def is an object) -> backup table -> UPDATE converting the 3 rows via SchemaContentFields' projection written in SQL -> DO/RAISE verify (0 legacy left; field-name sets equal old properties sets; every field has a source; required flags equal old required[]) -> ADD CONSTRAINT chk_input_schema_no_legacy_dialect CHECK (input_schema IS NULL OR NOT (input_schema ? 'properties')) + COMMENT. ROLLBACK sidecar drops the constraint FIRST then restores by id. Go: IsLegacyInputSchemaDialect (the constraint's predicate, wider than fromLegacy on purpose), a fourth birth check in store_generated_component, corrected doc comment + tripwire message/level, and TestLegacyDialectConversionMatchesProjection over the captured live before/after fixture (mutation-tested: a dropped required flag and an always-false predicate both fail it). Live the moment 437 is applied; the Go half is inert until the next chassis roll and needs no ordering (nothing in 437 names a Go affordance).
plan.risks: (1) A future LEGITIMATE use of a top-level 'properties' key on content_components.input_schema is refused — none exists (top-level key census over all 291 rows: 'properties' appears on exactly the 3 legacy rows) and the constraint's COMMENT says how to read a refusal. (2) The birth check refuses a generation the old code would have stored with render_mode='template' and an empty field set — that is a step failure where there was a silent mis-store; the component-creator has emitted 0 legacy schemas in 69 rows so the expected rate is ~0. (3) A restore from any bak_*/component_versions copy carrying the old dialect now fails on the constraint; the ROLLBACK sidecar drops it first. (4) The conversion pins the population by id; a fourth legacy row seeded between now and apply makes the guard REFUSE (safe), and the message says to re-census. (5) The three seeds 207/247/250 are not rewritten; a hand re-run of one now fails loudly rather than reintroducing the dialect. (6) store_generated_component_action.go carries a same-file passenger hunk from another lane (185: PageWantedLivePredicateFor at :890, uncommitted in the tree; the helper exists at HEAD so it compiles) — named in the commit message per the pathspec-passenger practice.

edits.rationale: The guarantee. The table is the only seam every producer of a legacy schema actually passed through (all four were hand SQL). Conversion first so the constraint can be added; projection mirrors the Go helper so no reader sees a different field set.
edits.sketch:
-- ── 1. Guards ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DO $$
DECLARE
  n_legacy   int;
  n_expected int;
  n_nonobj   int;
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
              WHERE conrelid = 'public.content_components'::regclass
                AND conname  = 'chk_input_schema_no_legacy_dialect') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'chk_input_schema_no_legacy_dialect already exists — migration 437 is already applied; record it with --record-only rather than re-running';
  END IF;

  SELECT count(*) INTO n_legacy FROM public.content_components WHERE input_schema ? 'properties';
  SELECT count(*) INTO n_expected FROM public.content_components
   WHERE input_schema ? 'properties'
     AND id IN ('fb870e82-2f01-46e4-9552-e764515e18d8',   -- evidence-timeseries
                'fa5e4524-e9e9-41f1-826a-8474c03c48e2',   -- mechanism-flow
                '5fe24e56-2526-469b-9554-1de39aa038b2');  -- report-dossier
  IF n_legacy <> 3 OR n_expected <> 3 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'legacy-dialect population is % rows (% of the 3 expected ids) — not the shape 437 was written against (3 rows: evidence-timeseries, mechanism-flow, report-dossier, measured 2026-08-16). Re-run the census, extend the conversion to the new rows, then apply', n_legacy, n_expected;
  END IF;

  -- Every property definition must be an object, or the projection below would error
  -- mid-statement rather than at this guard.
  SELECT count(*) INTO n_nonobj
    FROM public.content_components c, jsonb_each(c.input_schema->'properties') p
   WHERE c.input_schema ? 'properties' AND jsonb_typeof(p.value) <> 'object';
  IF n_nonobj <> 0 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION '% legacy property definition(s) are not JSON objects — extend the conversion before applying', n_nonobj;
...
-- ── 3. Convert: the SchemaContentFields projection, in SQL ──────────────────
UPDATE public.content_components c
   SET input_schema = jsonb_build_object('fields', (
         SELECT jsonb_object_agg(p.key,
                  -- the six keys the helper copies when present
                  (SELECT coalesce(jsonb_object_agg(k.key, k.value), '{}'::jsonb)
                     FROM jsonb_each(p.value) k
                    WHERE k.key IN ('source','on_missing','fallback','missing_reason','items','min_items'))
                  -- minItems → min_items, only when min_items itself is absent
               || CASE WHEN (p.value ? 'min_items') OR NOT (p.value ? 'minItems') THEN '{}'::jsonb
                       ELSE jsonb_build_object('min_items', p.value->'minItems') END
                  -- type: string-typed only; "string" becomes "text"
               || CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(p.value->'type') = 'string'
                       THEN jsonb_build_object('type', CASE WHEN p.value->>'type' = 'string' THEN 'text' ELSE p.value->>'type' END)
                       ELSE '{}'::jsonb END
                  -- llm_guidance from llm_guidance, else from description (non-empty strings only)
               || CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(p.value->'llm_guidance') = 'string' AND p.value->>'llm_guidance' <> ''
                       THEN jsonb_build_object('llm_guidance', p.value->>'llm_guidance')
                       WHEN jsonb_typeof(p.value->'description') = 'string' AND p.value->>'description' <> ''
                       THEN jsonb_build_object('llm_guidance', p.value->>'description')
                       ELSE '{}'::jsonb END
                  -- source defaults to "llm" when the property declares none
               || CASE WHEN p.value ? 'source' THEN '{}'::jsonb ELSE '{"source": "llm"}'::jsonb END
                  -- top-level required[] folded in
               || CASE WHEN c.input_schema->'required' ? p.key THEN '{"required": true}'::jsonb ELSE '{}'::jsonb END
                )
           FROM jsonb_each(c.input_schema->'properties') p
       )),
       updated_at = now()
 WHERE c.input_schema ? 'properties';

-- ── 4. Verify — RAISE, because a bare SELECT cannot stop the COMMIT ─────────
DO $$
DECLARE
...
-- ── 5. The guarantee ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ALTER TABLE public.content_components
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_input_schema_no_legacy_dialect
  CHECK (input_schema IS NULL OR NOT (input_schema ? 'properties'));

COMMENT ON CONSTRAINT chk_input_schema_no_legacy_dialect ON public.content_components IS
  'bugs_open/265, migration 437 (2026-08-16): input_schema must be the v2 {"fields":{...}} dialect. A top-level "properties" key is the retired JSON-Schema dialect and is refused for every producer (seeds, scripts, Go, admin). Nested properties under fields.<x>.items are fine. Reader: datahelpers.SchemaContentFields.';

Legibility at the one LLM producer: refuse before the write with the message that names the fix, instead of SQLSTATE 23514 after deriveRenderMode has mis-read the schema. Reuses the datahelpers predicate; no new classifier.

Proof that the SQL projection and the Go projection agree, over the live rows (fixture captured from a rolled-back probe run, not typed by hand), plus the predicate's verdicts on the shapes that matter. Mutation-tested both ways.
The three rows before (live 2026-08-16) and after (437's UPDATE, probe run rolled back). Re-capture, never re-type, if the projection changes.
